title: Training Notes on Patient Payment Plans Default Release and Reinstatement Terms
content:
Patient Services Center training notes on the tier figures that govern a defaulted Patient Payment Plans plan: where the released balance goes and how the plan may be reinstated.

| Tier | Released balance of a defaulted plan goes straight to the final notice | Times a defaulted plan may be reinstated over its life | Installments to be paid to reinstate | Reinstatement window (calendar days after default) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3-Month Interest-Free Plan | No | 1 | 1 | 30 |
| 6-Month Interest-Free Plan | No | 1 | 1 | 30 |
| 12-Month Interest-Free Plan | Yes | 1 | 1 | 30 |
| 18-Month Extended Plan | Yes | 1 | 2 | 30 |
| 24-Month Extended Plan | Yes | 1 | 2 | 30 |
| Financial Hardship Plan | No | 2 | 1 | 30 |

**Q. What does "goes straight to the final notice" mean in the table?**
A. Where the entry reads Yes, a defaulted plan's released balance goes straight to the final notice instead of restarting the statement series; where it reads No, the released balance restarts the statement series.

**Q. How many times may a defaulted plan be reinstated?**
A. Once over the plan's life on the 3-Month, 6-Month and 12-Month Interest-Free Plans and on the 18-Month and 24-Month Extended Plans; twice on the Financial Hardship Plan.

**Q. How many installments must be paid to reinstate?**
A. Two on the 18-Month Extended Plan and the 24-Month Extended Plan; one on every other tier.

**Q. How long after a default is reinstatement possible?**
A. Within 30 calendar days after the default on every tier.
